config.cxw.whatsapp.1.title: Have your phone at hand
config.cxw.whatsapp.1.body: Zaelar connects as a linked device of your WhatsApp, just like WhatsApp Web. Your messages never leave this computer. The next step shows a QR code to scan with your phone.
config.cxw.telegram.1.title: Go to my.telegram.org
config.cxw.telegram.1.body: Sign in with your phone number: the code arrives inside the Telegram app itself, not by SMS.
config.cxw.email.1.title: Create an app password
config.cxw.email.1.body: Your usual password won't work here. Gmail: turn on 2-Step Verification and create an app password in your Google account. Outlook: Security → Advanced options → App passwords. Another provider: the IMAP/SMTP password it gives you.
config.cxw.spotify.1.title: Sign in with your Spotify account
config.cxw.spotify.1.body: Pressing Connect opens Spotify so you can grant Zaelar access. Spotify requires Premium to control playback.
config.cxw.google.1.title: Create a Google Cloud project and enable {api}
config.cxw.google.1.body: In Google Cloud Console create a project (or use one of yours) and, under «APIs & Services → Library», enable {api}. On the «OAuth consent screen» choose «External» and publish it to production: in Testing mode Google disconnects the account every 7 days.
config.cxw.google.2.title: Create the OAuth client ID
config.cxw.google.2.body: Under «Credentials → Create credentials → OAuth client ID» choose «Web application» and add these authorized redirect URIs, one per service. Then copy the client ID (and the secret) for the next step.
config.cxw.onedrive.1.title: Register the app in Microsoft Entra
config.cxw.onedrive.1.body: In Microsoft Entra → App registrations → New registration: personal and organizational accounts, «Web» platform and this redirect URI.
config.cxw.onedrive.2.title: Copy the application ID
config.cxw.onedrive.2.body: On the app's page copy «Application (client) ID». If it asks for a secret, create one under «Certificates & secrets» and paste it too.
config.cxw.google_account.1.title: Put the OAuth client in your credentials
config.cxw.google_account.1.body: Download your OAuth client's client_secret_*.json from Google Cloud and drop it in Zaelar's .meshkore/credentials/ folder. It turns on Gmail, Calendar, Meet, Drive, Photos and YouTube at once; register these redirect URIs with Google.
config.cxw.architect.1.title: Copy the daemon token
config.cxw.architect.1.body: Copy the MeshKore daemon's access token. It is stored here, out of the model's reach, and you can revoke it any time.
config.cxw.meshkore.1.title: Have the cluster details at hand
config.cxw.meshkore.1.body: You need the name, the cluster_id and the token of the cluster you were invited to. The token never goes through the model.

config.cxw.telegram.2.title: Create the application
config.cxw.telegram.2.body: Open «API development tools» and fill in the form: App title «Zaelar», Short name «Zaelar», leave the rest blank. Press «Create application». You will see two values: the api_id (a short number) and the api_hash (a long string of letters and digits).
config.cxw.telegram.form_tip: Paste both values here. The api_id is a short number; the api_hash a long string of letters and digits.
config.cxw.telegram.missing: Something is missing: the api_id is digits only and the api_hash cannot be empty.

reset.confirm.body: All running processes will be STOPPED (browser searches, Brain Workers, widget creation), the desktop will be left blank and the widgets emptied: results, reports, charts and messaging content start from zero. Your memory, your credentials and connections (WhatsApp/Telegram/browser/email), your calendar —projects, tasks and appointments—, your language and the files the agent has saved are KEPT, unless you tick the boxes below.
reset.confirm.hint: Ticking any box restarts the server automatically (a few seconds). Your API keys and the model routing are never touched.

reset.confirm.wipeProfile: Start from SCRATCH, as if for the first time (wipes the LANGUAGE, the voice and the attention mode: when it comes back, Zaelar will ask which language you speak). It does not touch the installation’s models or voice providers.

connectors.amazon-music.why_not: Amazon publishes no playback API for third parties; the only API is invitation-only, for device makers.
connectors.amazon-photos.why_not: Amazon publishes no official API to read the Amazon Photos library; the only option is an unofficial cookie-based library that breaks its terms of service.
connectors.apple-photos.why_not: There is no public third-party API to read the iCloud Photos library; the same limit as iCloud Drive (CloudKit only exposes each app's private container).
connectors.deezer.why_not: Deezer closed its public API to new apps in November 2023; without an app registration there is no way in.
connectors.icloud-drive.why_not: CloudKit only exposes each app's private container; there is no public API to read a user's whole iCloud Drive.
connectors.soundcloud.why_not: Registration of new apps for its API has been closed for years (only a form with no guaranteed answer); without a client_id there is no search or streaming.
connectors.tidal.why_not: Its developer platform (2024) gives metadata and 30-second previews, not full playback for third parties.
connectors.youtube-music.why_not: YouTube Music has no public API; the free YouTube source (youtube-audio), which plays by default, already covers the real path.

config.catalog.fast.note: NON-reasoners only (the voice turn must close fast) and only benchmark-endorsed ones. deepseek-v4-pro DIRECT = production default (operator's norm, 2026-08-19: it is the titular and the only endpoint that actually obeys `thinking:disabled`). deepseek-v4-flash routed 12/12 in §9. The broker entries carry the `deepseek/` prefix and the direct ones do not — that is the provider's catalog, not a typo. Endpoint comes from the provider: there is no URL to type.
config.catalog.fast.provider.deepseek.la: DeepSeek DIRECT (production default — the only one that truly stops reasoning)
config.catalog.fast.provider.aimlapi.lab: AIMLAPI (broker — the one account we manage)
config.catalog.fast.provider.groq.label: Groq (cloud, fastest — routes worse)
config.catalog.code_agent.note: Headless agent that drives jobs (memory/web/code). Per-job-type model optional. Each provider serves ONLY its own models. Pick a preset to move CLI + endpoint + model together.
config.catalog.code_agent.provider.claud: Can restrict Bash to our bridges only (single-writer invariant) → the only backend valid for untrusted input (deny_tools) and cluster dev workers. The glm-*/kimi-* entries belong to the relay tiers (Z.AI / Moonshot subscription plans): they only work while that endpoint is the active tier — see workers/providers.py.
config.catalog.code_agent.provider.codex: Has NO tool allowlist — only sandbox modes, so a Codex worker runs a full shell (wider blast radius). Refused for untrusted input and dev workers.
config.catalog.code_agent.provider.grok_: Same wire format AND same allowlist syntax as Claude Code — verified it enforces `--deny Bash(...)`, so it CAN hold the single-writer invariant (unlike Codex). Pay-per-token: watch the cost, a trivial turn already costs ~$0.03 (large system prompt).
Subscription plan with a WEEKLY quota: when it runs out, everything on this tier stops at once — that is what the relay chain exists for.
config.catalog.code_agent.preset.cc_deep: ⚠️ Its gateway does NOT map Claude aliases — that belief is what shipped this rung broken. Verified against the live endpoint: a Claude alias gets `400 — The supported API model names are deepseek-v4-pro or deepseek-v4-flash`. Use the DeepSeek name. Compatible in the PROTOCOL is not compatible in the CATALOG. Cheapest of the three.
Native xAI agent CLI. Grok 4.6 ($2/$6 per Mtok, 500k ctx, reasoning) is selectable as the model if quality beats cost.
pay-per-token — measured ~$0.03 for a trivial turn
config.catalog.code_agent.preset.cc_loca: LOCAL ONLY — a browser login does not exist inside a container, so this tier cannot be the cloud's coverage. It is the last rung of the relay chain.
config.catalog.memory_processor.note: Off-hot-path (does not touch voice latency) but WRITE-COMPLETENESS is the nº1 lever of recall. BENCHMARKED 2026-08-09 (21 candidates × 34 cases, see zaelar-model-benchmarks.md §12.3): deepseek-v4-flash ties gpt-4.1-mini on capture (98.5 vs 98.9%) and precision (100%) for −55% cost → CHOSEN; fallback gemini-2.5-flash → gpt-4.1-mini. ⛔ gpt-4o-mini is VETOED: it files an allergy under slot=operator.diet, and a slot invalidates every earlier pill with that slot — a later diet change would erase the allergy. bench.mod.fast.label: Fast brain · FlashBrain
bench.mod.fast.role: Answers EVERY voice/chat turn in real time: small talk, tool-calling (show/close widgets, search, music, memory, escalate) — it can never reason (thinking OFF); the turn must close in ~1-3 s or the voice goes silent.
bench.mod.fast.why: CHANGE 2026-07-31 (previous primary → DeepSeek V4 Flash non-thinking): robust A/B (tests/voice/e2e/agent/model_bench, 16 unambiguous turns ×4 reps, same real prompt+tools) → deepseek non-thinking ROUTING 10/10 (vs 8/10 for the previous one, which UNDER-acted: it did not look up schedules or add the appointment), INTEL 6/6 (after narrowing the 'insists→execute' rule that made it over-act on meta/contradiction — fix flash/prompt.py 3bd8c29), TTFT p50 1170 ms (vs 1821 ms for the previous one) and ~7x cheaper. The MODE matters: v4-flash THINKS by default (over-acts, +latency) → fast_client forces thinking:disabled when the model is deepseek. The emergency fallback points at the SAME primary. [HISTORY] Earlier A/B (grok-4-fast-non-reasoning): grok 'seemed dumb' — it did not search when it should (it hallucinated), did not introspect its own contradiction and reacted with spurious actions to meta questions. The primary of the time searched reliably and explained instead of acting on doubts, at comparable latency.
bench.mod.fast.hallucination_note: Grok (xAI) is STILL banned from this seat: in tests it mixes memory↔widget_data and answers 'Done' to questions that were not orders — the most expensive failure in a non-reasoning brain is acting confidently on a misunderstanding.
bench.mod.memory_processor.label: Memory · write HEART
bench.mod.memory_processor.role: Distils every turn into pills (fact + metadata + layer + slot). Off-hot-path (never touches voice latency) — but WRITE-COMPLETENESS is the nº1 lever of recall (V2-031): no retriever can recover a fact that was written badly.
bench.mod.memory_processor.why: Chosen on PRICE at equal useful quality: 21 commercial candidates × 34 cases × 4 axes, 3 passes for the finalists. It ties the previous primary (gpt-4.1-mini) on the two axes that destroy data — capturing the fact (98.5% vs 98.9%: one fact in 90) and not polluting with discards (100% both) — at roughly half the price. Writing is off-hot-path, so its slower speed costs the voice turn nothing.
bench.mod.memory_processor.hallucination: gpt-4o-mini is even cheaper ($0.567) and is VETOED: with an allergy stated in English it sets slot=operator.diet (3/3 passes). A slot invalidates everything earlier with that slot, so a future «I'm vegetarian now» would erase the allergy — silent data loss. The distiller is chosen by the bench, never by the provider's reputation (this repealed the old «memory = always OpenAI» rule).
bench.mod.memory_rem.label: Memory · REM sleep (consolidation)
bench.mod.memory_rem.role: Once a day it groups durable memories by concept and distils 1 high-level INSIGHT per group (kind='insight'). It is what makes the memory LEARN patterns instead of just piling up facts. Fully off-hot-path: it runs before dawn.
bench.mod.memory_rem.why: Here QUALITY rules, not price, and that comes from the shape of the code: ALL groups go in ONE call, capped at 8 groups × 12 memories, once a day — the cost does NOT grow with the size of the memory. Across all candidates the yearly cost was negligible, so optimising price here would be optimising noise. deepseek-v4-flash scores 97.8-99% and is the one that best keeps names and figures when summarising (98.4-100%), which is the data that can truly be lost.
bench.mod.memory_rem.hallucination_note: The previous primary (gpt-4.1-mini) failed the axis the old bench did not measure: given a group of trivia («had a coffee», «forgot where the keys were») it ALWAYS made up an insight, 0% correct in 3 passes — turning a slip into a durable trait of the operator. Staying quiet when there is no pattern is part of the job. The more POWERFUL models (v4-pro, reasoner, gpt-4.1) do NOT do better: the job is mechanical and reasoning only adds verbosity.
bench.mod.triage.label: Messaging triage (WhatsApp/Telegram)
bench.mod.triage.role: Classifies the relevance of incoming messages — a simple job, NOT tool-routing.
bench.mod.triage.why: Simple classification (no action routing) → grok is fine here, even though it is banned from the FlashBrain. With a remote model the message content leaves the machine; a local endpoint keeps it local.
bench.mod.susurro.label: «Susurro» — conversational auditor
bench.mod.susurro.role: Completely outside the voice path: it reviews stretches with friction (complaint/repetition/failure) and returns corrections from a closed catalog. Here it CAN be a reasoner.
bench.mod.susurro.why: The MODEL is still not chosen with data — its benchmark is still pending (§10 of the dense doc), and that holds for the current one as much as for the previous one. On 2026-08-09 the PATH changed: it went through OpenAI directly, a credential a container deployment may not hold, so there it would have failed silently; it moved to the broker with the same model. On 2026-08-21 the MODEL changed: `openai/gpt-4.1-mini` could no longer be what runs by default (operator's rule, already written in the i18n rung of `memllm._FAILOVER`). It stays in the CATALOG for self-hosters who want it: what the rule forbids is that it runs without anyone choosing it, not that it exists.
bench.mod.i18n.label: Translating the interface into a new language
bench.mod.i18n.role: The first time someone speaks a language that does not ship built in (only English and Spanish are PRESET), a model translates the 514 interface texts. It runs once per language, during setup — never during a conversation.
bench.mod.i18n.why: Here RELIABILITY rules, not price: it is paid ONCE per language (11 batches, a few cents) and a failed batch leaves 50 interface texts in English, with no second pass to fix them. The August probe (§12.5) had ruled DeepSeek out for this job because it OVER-reasoned —6-8 times the tokens it delivered, 50-60 s per batch—, but that measurement was of the FLASH model served by the BROKER, which is exactly where the reasoning switch is accepted and ignored. On its own endpoint it IS obeyed, so the reason for ruling it out disappears with the endpoint change. If it over-reasons again, it gets measured and changed with the measurement in hand.
bench.mod.cluster.label: Cluster channel (conversation with other agents, off-voice)
bench.mod.cluster.role: The SAME FlashBrain engine on an untrusted profile, off-voice tier — it does not have the latency pressure of the synchronous voice turn, so it can be somewhat slower/more powerful.
bench.mod.cluster.why: It used to go through AIMLAPI (an aggregator with a markup). It now calls Z.AI's Anthropic-compatible endpoint (/v1/messages) directly; verified end-to-end with `tests/cluster/e2e/run_cluster_suite.py` — faster than the previous AIMLAPI route.
bench.mod.code_agent.label: Brain Workers (the long work: research, browse, write code)
bench.mod.code_agent.role: Every escalated job is a headless worker that REASONS with its own tools for minutes, outside the voice turn. These are TWO decisions, not one: who DRIVES (the CLI) and who REASONS (endpoint + model). That is why they are chosen as a PRESET — moving them separately produces mismatches that do not fail on save, but minutes later inside an already-dead job.
bench.mod.code_agent.why: Serialised bench of 2026-08-13 on a job with several chained pieces (ferry + hotel + restaurant, with a link and price per piece and the obligation to mark anything unconfirmed as PROVISIONAL). Claude Code + Z.AI completed it: 12 min, 10 proposals on the results sheet, the ferry CONFIRMED with a source and what could not be confirmed (exact times, which live in the booking engine) marked as provisional instead of made up — which is exactly the axis that separates a worker that researches from one that writes something plausible. And it did it with the relay's web search EXHAUSTED: Z.AI's MCP quota was used up, so it went at the websites one by one with WebFetch, ate 403s from DirectFerries/Booking/Baleària and kept going. A candidate that only works with good search is no good for production.
bench.mod.code_agent.hallucination_note: The quality axis here is NOT eloquence: it is whether it flags what it could not confirm. A worker that fills in a ferry time it did not find produces a delivery that looks BETTER and is worth less than nothing, because the operator would use it to book.
